reviews.text:
I really only want to write positive reviews, and I've never written a negative one even when I've had a bad experience, but I'll write one now.

The male nurses are incredibly unfriendly.

This time it was urgent, and other hospitals were closed, so I went to this one since it didn't require an appointment.

This wasn't my first time. I didn't have a bad experience last time, which is why I went again, but this time was different.

The other nurses also seemed bored when answering the phone, so if you don't want to have a bad experience at a hospital, you should probably avoid going. (laughs)
The male nurses are the worst, but the other female nurses (I don't know who they are) are similar.

If you can't treat all dogs equally, then maybe you should quit your job working with people?

I don't even want to give it one star.
My dog ​​barks quite a bit, so it bothers other people, and I usually wait outside the hospital. However, after the examination, my dog ​​had calmed down, and I was only waiting to pay, so I went inside. Suddenly, a male staff member snatched my dog ​​from me without saying a word. I was completely confused and didn't understand what was happening. I was called to pay, and my dog ​​was nowhere to be seen, which made me anxious. Then, they explained the medication, and after listening to it, they said, "The explanation will be long and your dog is noisy, so we asked you to stay here." Honestly, I don't understand why they took him from my arms without saying a word, and the explanation was only about a minute long, so I wondered if all that was really necessary.
Also, at another hospital, they said my dog ​​had a heart murmur during a health checkup, but here they said there was nothing wrong and he was healthy. They said his heart sounds were fine. That's a misdiagnosis. It's close to my house, so it's easy to go there, but as long as the doctor and the male nurse are there, I will not go back.

I was extremely angry with the way this was handled.
I took my dog ​​to the vet for an eye tumor and corneal abnormality, but they only continued to prescribe eye drops and wait and see, and the symptoms did not improve. Because my dog ​​couldn't open its eye, I became worried and decided to find a specialized animal ophthalmology clinic in Toyonaka City myself.
When I called to request a referral, I told the receptionist (Ms. Shindo) the name of the hospital, but she said, "It would be troublesome if I made a mistake," which surprised me greatly. If she didn't know the hospital name, she could have looked it up on the spot. I wish they had made an effort to connect me to a specialist hospital more smoothly, rather than putting an unnecessary burden on the owner.
Furthermore, Dr. Kawabe, the hospital director, was reluctant to make a referral. However, if treatment is not improving and it is difficult to handle at their own clinic, isn't it an important role of a veterinarian to refer the dog to a specialist hospital as soon as possible?
In reality, when I contacted the specialized animal ophthalmology clinic in Toyonaka City, they said, "A phone call from Shinsaibashi Animal Hospital is all we need." And it was only after the specialist clinic contacted them directly that I was finally able to get a referral.

My beloved dog was in tears and unable to open its eyes. Because of this situation, I wish they had referred us to a specialist more quickly. From this series of actions, I didn't feel that the animal's well-being was the top priority, which was very disappointing.

I believe that minimizing the burden on pet owners and promptly referring difficult cases to specialists are also important aspects of medical care.

Having been a patient for eight years, I was extremely indignant about this response.

As a pet owner, this was an unacceptable response. In a situation involving the life of a beloved family member, this response felt incredibly irresponsible.

This was the most distrustful experience I've ever had.

I will never use this hospital again.

I hope my experience will serve as a reference for other pet owners considering this hospital.

It was the worst; this hospital only cares about making money.
The puppy that passed away this time was born at this hospital 15 years and 8 months ago. Dr. Takeuchi had been taking care of the puppy since it was a mother, but he was transferred last year, and since it was far away, we had no choice but to go to this hospital. The puppy had been taking kidney medication since last year, but this year it developed inflammation, and we had tests done once a week. The type of medication hadn't changed, and we had tests done again. Do they really take blood from a puppy weighing less than 2 kg every week? Even humans don't do that. For the past week, she hasn't eaten anything at all, so we did a blood test and an ultrasound that day. From that day on, she received IV fluids every day, but two days later, we did another blood test, and on the third day, they tried to do another ultrasound. I was so angry that they couldn't do anything but keep doing tests that I refused the ultrasound. Two days later, they recommended liquid food, so I bought some and forced her to drink it with a syringe, but the next day she had diarrhea. I think it must have been even more painful for a baby that weighs only 1.4 kg to have diarrhea. In the end, she passed away last night, but I think they couldn't do anything more than give her IV fluids every day for eight days, and I'm so angry at the doctors who just keep doing tests.
I take my cat, Laala, to the groomer for nail trims and brushing. I'm very happy with the kind groomer! Even my rambunctious Laala is happy!

I wouldn't even give it one star.
In April, my cat had fleas, so I applied Frontline at home.
I was worried about any skin abnormalities, so I took her to the vet.
The vet did a quick visual inspection and determined there were no fleas.
They explained that instead of buying the medication that day, it would be covered by insurance if I came back the following month and the vet applied it.
When I went back in May, a different vet explained that we should decide on the medication for prevention after discussing it.
They then explained that after their previous explanation, they had re-checked and found that insurance coverage would be difficult.
If that's the case, shouldn't they have contacted me then?
Considering the stress on my indoor cat from unnecessary outings, I could have simply bought the medication myself.
I was extremely displeased, so I told them I would buy the medication at a different hospital and left. I will never go there again.
The staff's attitude was absolutely terrible; I'm never coming back a second time.

My beloved cat was brought to the vet with severe dehydration due to stomatitis, but basic procedures such as taking her temperature, listening to her with a stethoscope, and checking her oral cavity were not performed during the examination. Without any explanation of the prognosis (whether she was critically ill or had a chance of recovery), intravenous fluids were started without any clear plan.

When I inquired about hospitalization with Dr. Kawabe, he said, "She might die during hospitalization, is that alright?" As a pet owner, there was no way I could agree to that. If the situation was so difficult to handle, shouldn't they have referred me to an appropriate secondary care facility or a large hospital?

Afterward, I transferred her to another hospital, where she was able to receive proper hospitalization and treatment. The treatment at the previous hospital was far from a fundamental solution.
The always thorough examinations and state-of-the-art equipment give me peace of mind.
I was asked by an acquaintance of mine to take his kitty for a checkup, and the doctor explained everything to me in a way that was easy to understand.

My 13-year-old male Persian cat was born in January of this year. Dr. Kawabe, who was new to the hospital, performed surgery to remove the tip of his penis after a kidney stone blocked his urethra, preventing him from urinating on his own. He also performed a beautiful procedure on the scar. I thought he would either die or urinate for the rest of his life, but he started using the litter box like a normal cat and is incredibly healthy. I wish I had performed the surgery when he was younger. The doctor is kind, polite, and humble, and he loves animals in general. The hospital staff and nurses are also highly professional and love animals, so I think this is a trustworthy hospital. The cost was also reasonable. Thank you very much.
It's clean and the reception staff are very friendly. I'm satisfied with both the treatment and the clinic.

Dr. Okamoto's examinations are accurate and he's very caring, and the nurses are incredibly kind too 💓
I feel completely at ease leaving my pet in his care 😊 I'm so glad I found a veterinarian like Dr. Okamoto❣️ …

Misdiagnosis is common.
I had my cat under her care, but no matter how many times I complained about the symptoms, she was just told not to worry and didn't do anything in particular.
To top it off, she flatly declared it wasn't cat flu and instead looked at me suspiciously, as if to say, "Did you do something to my cat?" which was very unpleasant.
The symptoms didn't improve, so I went to another hospital and was diagnosed with cat flu. I was glad there was no adhesion in the eye, but I never want that female doctor to treat me again.

The doctors and other staff are nice, but the male nurse's attitude is too friendly.

When he asked me why I was there, he said with a half-smile, "You're back again? These kinds of symptoms often occur due to stress." When I asked, "So, should I not have come?", he replied, "That's not what I meant..." I come to the hospital because I'm anxious, and the thought that they think I've come for something trivial again makes me hesitant to continue my visits.
The doctors and nurses are kind and caring!

We've been going to this clinic since our baby was little, and the doctors and nurses are all so kind and attentive that we can relax even while waiting in the waiting room! Thank you so much for everything!
I have always been treated by Director Takeuchi. This time it was a different doctor, so when I checked his Instagram I found out he was transferred in June. I am very shocked and saddened.

I visited because my pet cat was unwell.

The receptionist's attitude was poor, and the female doctor who examined my cat only used technical jargon, making it difficult to understand my questions. She then inexplicably referred me to another affiliated hospital, which made me suspicious. When I took my cat to that hospital, it was immediately admitted.

The doctor who examined my cat and the receptionist were saying completely different things, and the receptionist even blamed me, implying it was my fault for letting my cat become ill.
The doctor was kind and gave me a thorough examination and explained the test results, which made me feel at ease.

Everyone there is so caring and attentive, so I feel completely at ease leaving my pet in their care.

I also entrust all of my pet's grooming to them.

Thank you for your continued support! ✨
The teachers are all so nice, so I feel at ease using your services. 🙇‍♂️
Thank you for your continued support! …
A very kind veterinarian will examine your pet carefully.

He is a doctor who always takes good care of the animals and thinks about them.
The nurses are also very kind and you can tell they love animals, so you can leave your pet there with peace of mind.
They also have a salon on site, so even pets with chronic illnesses can be groomed with peace of mind.
They also have their own insurance, so it was very helpful that they were able to admit pets with chronic illnesses.
The facilities are well-equipped and, above all, the doctors are highly skilled, so I can recommend them with confidence.

This is a good hospital that I've been going to for many years and can trust completely.

The doctors and staff are all very kind.

I've been bringing my dog ​​to this clinic for over 10 years, ever since he was a puppy.

The doctor and all the staff are always kind and caring, making it a very trustworthy clinic.
This is my first time using your services. You are very kind and provide genuine, heartfelt support.

The nurses and veterinarians listened attentively and treated the animals with love and care. I also appreciate that they accept card payments.

They have very few days off, which was a real lifesaver.

Although it's a bit of a distance from my home, the doctor is very kind and reassuring during examinations.

I look forward to continuing to use their services in the future.

My child is a picky eater, vomits easily, and has a chronic epilepsy condition, but they are treated very carefully. The phone service is also very polite, and we have been taking care of our 11-year-old child ever since.
The location was easy to find on the main street, and the consultation was quick, which was great.
Despite the busy holiday season, I was able to receive treatment with peace of mind thanks to your courteous service. Thank you for answering my questions appropriately.🙇‍♂️´- …
My 15-year-old Chihuahua is always well cared for here. Since starting the medication, his seizures and epileptic symptoms have calmed down.
I'm so glad the teacher listened carefully and was so supportive!

The clinic is clean, and the doctor is kind and attentive.

However, the long waiting times are a real pain.
They always provide kind and thorough examinations, and explain the symptoms clearly.
